concerns.text: The plan explicitly states the study is 'observational' and claims will be 'associational', yet the methodology involves *programmatically generating* Low/Med/High entropy variants (FR-001) by reordering commands and substituting tokens. This is an experimental manipulation of the independent variable, not a passive observation. If the plan intends to claim a causal link between 'complexity' and 'degradation', the design supports it; if it intends to claim only correlation, the experimental design is over-engineered. The current text creates a contradiction between the active manipulation described in FR-001 and the passive 'observational' label in 2.3.

The method for generating 'Low Entropy' variants ('reorder commands to be repetitive') risks destroying the semantic validity of the interaction log. If the reordered commands no longer form a coherent instruction sequence, the resulting video generation failure may be due to *semantic incoherence* rather than *sequence complexity* (entropy). The plan lacks a control or validation step to ensure that 'Low Entropy' variants remain semantically plausible instructions, threatening the construct validity of the 'Complexity Score' as a predictor of model failure.

The plan targets ~1.5k inference runs (289 cases × 3 variants × ~5 models) on GitHub Actions Free Tier (2 CPU, ~7GB RAM) within 6 hours. World model inference (even CPU-optimized) is computationally intensive. Running 1.5k video generations in 6 hours on 2 CPUs implies ~2.4 seconds per video generation including I/O and overhead. This is likely physically impossible for current world models, suggesting the sample size or runtime constraints are infeasible, which invalidates the power analysis and the ability to detect the intended effect.
